questions.prompt: The parents of a 2-year-old child with short bowel syndrome are concerned about their child's nutrition. Which of the following is an appropriate recommendation by the nurse?
options: The child should consume a high-fiber diet.
The child may require parenteral nutrition.
The child should avoid all fats in the diet.
The child should consume more dairy products.
questions.rationale: Short bowel syndrome can lead to malabsorption of nutrients. In severe cases, parenteral nutrition may be required to ensure the child receives adequate nutrition. A high-fiber diet (option A) may not be appropriate as it can increase stool output. Avoiding all fats (option C) is not recommended as some fat is necessary for growth and development. While some children with short bowel syndrome may tolerate dairy products (option D), others may not due to lactose intolerance.

questions.prompt: A patient presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of sharp, severe chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient's blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, heart rate is 120 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 90%. What should the nurse suspect?

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?

questions.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. This often results in projectile vomiting after feeding. Severe diarrhea (option B), frequent loose stools (option C), and abdominal distension (option D) are not typically associated with pyloric stenosis.

questions.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis is started on a regimen of multiple antibiotics. What should the nurse include in patient teaching regarding this treatment?

questions.rationale: Tuberculosis requires a prolonged treatment with multiple antibiotics, often for several months. questions.rationale: All of these actions are important nursing responsibilities before a corneal transplant. questions.prompt: A nurse is providing dietary education to the parents of a child with celiac disease. Which food should the nurse instruct the parents to eliminate from the child's diet?
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Gluten is found in wheat, rye, and barley. Therefore, wheat should be eliminated from the diet of a child with celiac disease. Rice (option A), corn (option C), and potatoes (option D) are naturally gluten-free and can be included in the diet.

questions.rationale: These symptoms indicate a severe asthma attack and the patient is at risk of respiratory failure. The nurse should administer oxygen to increase oxygen saturation and notify the physician immediately for further intervention.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient who may have a perforated eardrum. Which of the following symptoms would likely be present?
questions.rationale: A perforated eardrum can cause ringing in the ears (tinnitus), sudden cessation of ear pain (as the pressure is relieved by the perforation), and hearing loss. Therefore, all of these symptoms might be present if a patient has a perforated eardrum.

Administering a diuretic as ordered by the physician

Providing emotional support to the patient

questions.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis is started on a regimen of multiple antibiotics. What should the nurse include in patient teaching regarding this treatment?

The patient should not drink alcohol while on these medications
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis requires a prolonged treatment with multiple antibiotics, often for several months. It's also important to inform the patient that although they might feel better, they need to finish the full course of antibiotics to fully treat the infection.

questions.rationale: Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber indicates a possible air leak in the system. The nurse should assess the chest tube, connections, and drainage system for leaks.

questions.prompt: Question: A nurse is providing education to a group of parents about preventing head lice (pediculosis). Which of the following instructions should the nurse include?
options: Share hats and combs to build immunity.
Use a special shampoo for lice every day.
Check the child's hair regularly for lice and nits.
Shave the child's head if lice are found.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Check the child's hair regularly for lice and nits. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Select all the correct statements about educating the patient with heart failure.
options: It is important patients with heart failure notify their physician if they gain more than 6 pounds in a day or 10 pounds in a week.
Patients with heart failure should receive an annual influenza vaccine and be up-to-date with the pneumonia vaccine.
Heart failure patients should limit sodium intake to 2-3 grams per day.
Heart failure is exacerbated by illness, too much fluid or sodium intake, and arrhythmias.
questions.rationale: Correct option: It is important patients with heart failure notify their physician if they gain more than 6 pounds in a day or 10 pounds in a week. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child weighing 50 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 5 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 83 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient presents with a sudden loss of vision in one eye. The nurse recognizes this as a possible sign of: a) Glaucoma b) Cataract c) Macular degeneration d) Retinal detachment Answer: d) Retinal detachment 18. A patient complains of sudden vision loss in the right eye. The nurse knows that this could be a symptom of which of the following conditions?
questions.rationale: Sudden vision loss is often associated with retinal detachment. Macular degeneration (A) typically causes a gradual loss of central vision. Glaucoma (B) usually causes peripheral vision loss over time. Cataracts (D) cause a gradual loss of overall vision clarity, not sudden vision loss.

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of neuropathy. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer pain medication (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

blocks.text: **Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention** is a core competency within **Week 16: Psychiatric Mental Health, Crisis Care & Psychotherapeutic Medications** for the Next-Generation NCLEX-RN (NGN). This lesson synthesizes high-yield pathophysiology, bedside nursing priorities, pharmacology safety, and test-taking rules triangulated across **Saunders Comprehensive Review (9th Ed.)**, **Kaplan NCLEX-RN Prep**, and **LaCharity Prioritization, Delegation, and Assignment**.

**Clinical Judgment Priority:** Always assess the client first when vital signs or acute symptoms change, unless immediate life-saving intervention (airway clearance, oxygen, chest compressions, or stopping an offending infusion) is required first.

items: Phases of a therapeutic nurse–client relationship
Therapeutic Communication Process
Therapeutic Techniques
Closed-ended questions -Questions that ask for specific information such as a “yes” or “no” answer and therefore inhibit communication
Nontherapeutic Techniques

Coping mechanisms- Coping involves any effort to decrease anxiety. Coping mechanisms can be constructive or destructive, task- or problem-oriented in relation to direct problem solving, cognitively oriented in an attempt to neutralize the meaning of the problem, or defense- or emotion-oriented, thus regulating the response to protect oneself.

Defense mechanisms- As anxiety increases, the individual copes by using defense mechanisms. A defense mechanism is a coping mechanism used in an effort to protect the individual from feelings of anxiety; as anxiety increases and becomes overwhelming, the individual copes by using defense mechanisms to protect the ego and decrease anxiety
Coping and Defense Mechanisms

Milieu therapy - The milieu refers to the safe physical and social environment in which an individual is receiving treatment. Safety is the most important priority in managing the milieu, and all encounters with the client have the goal of being “therapeutic.” One-to-one relationships are used to examine client behaviors, feelings, and interactions within the context of the therapeutic group activities.

Interpersonal psychotherapy- A treatment modality that uses a therapeutic relationship to modify the client’s feelings, attitudes, and behaviors and that works within an agreed-upon time frame to help meet the client’s goals

9. Educate the client about evidence-based therapeutic interventions, such as medications, cognitive behavioral therapy, prolonged exposure therapy, and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR).

Rationale: Responding to the feelings expressed by a client is an effective therapeutic communication technique. The correct option is an example of the use of restating. The remaining options block communication because they minimize the client’s experience and do not facilitate exploration of the client’s expressed feelings. In addition, use of the word why is nontherapeutic because clients frequently interpret why questions as accusations. Why questions can cause resentment, insecurity and mistrust

Rationale: The correct option uses the therapeutic communication technique of exploring. Exploring is an important technique to use in examining experiences that are important to the client. The remaining options are nontherapeutic responses and are blocks to communication. Additionally, they do not encourage the client to expand on the problem. The response “Really?” can be interpreted by the client that the nurse is doubtful of what the client has expressed. Use of the word why is nontherapeutic because it may be interpreted as accusatory and can cause insecurity and mistrust. Offering personal experiences moves the focus away from the client and onto the nurse

Rationale: Restating is a therapeutic communication technique in which the nurse repeats what the client says to show understanding and to review what was said. Although it is appropriate for the nurse to attempt to assess the client’s ability to discuss feelings openly with family members, it does not help the client discuss the feelings causing the anger. The nurse’s direct attempt to expect the client to talk more about the anger is premature. The nurse would never make a judgment regarding the reason for the client’s feeling; this is nontherapeutic in the one-to-one relationship.

Rationale: It is most therapeutic for the nurse to empathize with the client’s experience. The remaining options lack this connection with the client. Disagreeing with delusions may make the client more defensive, and the client may cling to the delusions even more. Encouraging discussion regarding the delusion is inappropriate.

Rationale: Clients who are withdrawn may be immobile and mute and may require consistent, repeated approaches. Communication with withdrawn clients requires much patience from the nurse. Interventions include the establishment of interpersonal contact. The nurse facilitates communication with the client by sitting in silence, asking simple open-ended questions rather than direct questions, and pausing to provide opportunities for the client to respond. Although overstimulation is not appropriate, there is no therapeutic value in ignoring the client. The client’s safety is not the responsibility of other clients.
PSYCHOTHERAPEUTIC MEDICATIONS

Concurrent use with amphetamines, antidepressants, dopamine, epinephrine, levodopa/carbidopa, nasal decongestants, norepinephrine, tyramine-containing foods, or vasoconstrictors may cause hypertensive crisis.

Hypertensive crisis – Hypertension, Occipital headache radiating frontally, Neck stiffness and soreness, Nausea and vomiting, Sweating Fever and chills, Clammy skin, Dilated pupils, Palpitations, tachycardia, or bradycardia, Constricting chest pain
Antidote for hypertensive crisis: Phentolamine by intravenous injection

quiz.prompt: The parents of a child diagnosed with sickle cell disease ask how they can prevent a crisis. What is the nurse's best response?
options: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures."
"Your child should avoid all physical activity."
"Give your child aspirin if they complain of pain."
"Make sure your child eats a high-fat diet."
quiz.rationale: Correct option: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following interventions would be most beneficial for this patient?
quiz.rationale: Increased fluid intake can help thin out thick secretions in the lungs, making them easier to cough up and improving oxygenation.

quiz.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a corticosteroid inhaler and a bronchodilator inhaler. How should these medications be administered?
options: The bronchodilator should be used, followed by the corticosteroid
The corticosteroid should be used, followed by the bronchodilator
Both inhalers should be used simultaneously
The order of administration does not matter
quiz.rationale: The bronchodilator should be administered first to open the airways, allowing the corticosteroid to be more effectively delivered and absorbed.

quiz.prompt: Question: A child with idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) is admitted to the hospital. Which intervention should be included in the child's care plan?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Monitoring for signs of bleeding (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A patient with heart failure is experiencing shortness of breath. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Administer oxygen (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant on a pediatric oncology unit. Which task is appropriate to delegate?
options: Discussing the side effects of chemotherapy with a patient's parents
Administering oral pain medication to a child with bone cancer
Assisting a child with leukemia with bathing and dressing
Assessing a child's response to a blood transfusion
quiz.rationale: Option C is an appropriate task to delegate to a nursing assistant as it falls within their scope of practice. Options A, B, and D involve patient education, medication administration, and assessment, respectively, which are within the nurse's scope of practice and should not be delegated.

quiz.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis is started on a regimen of multiple antibiotics. What should the nurse include in patient teaching regarding this treatment?
options: The patient will need to be on antibiotics for several weeks
The patient should expect a rapid improvement in symptoms
The patient should not drink alcohol while on these medications
quiz.rationale: Tuberculosis requires a prolonged treatment with multiple antibiotics, often for several months. The patient should be cautioned not to drink alcohol while on these medications due to potential for liver damage. It's also important to inform the patient that although they might feel better, they need to finish the full course of antibiotics to fully treat the infection.

quiz.prompt: A patient with hypoparathyroidism is experiencing seizures. What is the nurse's first action?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Administer calcium supplements (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A client with pneumonia is prescribed incentive spirometry. What is the rationale for this intervention?
options: To assess the client's respiratory rate
To measure the client's peak expiratory flow rate
To improve the client's lung expansion and prevent atelectasis
To monitor the client's oxygen saturation levels
quiz.rationale: Incentive spirometry is used to improve lung expansion, prevent atelectasis (collapse of the lung), and promote deep breathing. It helps to improve ventilation and oxygenation, especially in clients with pneumonia who may have decreased lung function

quiz.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is experiencing dry skin and hair loss. What is the nurse's first action?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Increase levothyroxine dose (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A patient with acromegaly is taking octreotide. What is the primary goal of treatment?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Decrease growth hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been prescribed a liquid medication. The prescription calls for 5 mL to be given twice daily. The parents are unsure how to measure this amount. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Use a teaspoon from the kitchen.
Use the dropper that came with the medication.
Use a syringe without a needle.
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Use a syringe without a needle. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is administering eardrops to an adult client. Which of the following is the correct method?
options: Instil the drops directly onto the eardrum
Instil the drops onto the wall of the ear canal
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted towards the affected ear
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted away from the affected ear
quiz.rationale: When administering eardrops, the client's head should be tilted so that the affected ear is facing upward. This allows the medication to travel down the ear canal. Options A and B are incorrect because the drops should not be instilled directly onto the eardrum or the wall of the ear canal as this can cause discomfort and potentially damage the eardrum. Option C is incorrect because tilting the head towards the affected ear may cause the medication to drain out of the ear canal.

quiz.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is 2 days post-op from a thoracotomy. The patient is reluctant to perform deep breathing exercises due to pain. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement?
options: Administer pain medication before the exercises
Encourage shallow breathing to prevent discomfort
Discontinue the exercises until the pain subsides
Encourage the patient to hold their breath as long as possible
quiz.rationale: Deep breathing exercises are critical after thoracotomy to prevent complications such as pneumonia and atelectasis. Administering pain medication before the exercises can help alleviate the patient's discomfort and encourage compliance.

quiz.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is taking methimazole. What is the primary goal of treatment?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Increase thyroid hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A child with osteosarcoma reports pain in the affected leg. The nurse has delegated the administration of oral pain medication to a nursing assistant. What is the most appropriate action by the nurse?
options: The nurse should administer the medication instead
The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration
The nurse should instruct the nursing assistant to assess the child's pain level
The nurse should document the administration of the medication
quiz.rationale: The nurse cannot delegate the administration of medication or the assessment of pain to a nursing assistant. These tasks fall within the nurse's scope of practice. The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration to determine the effectiveness of the medication.

quiz.prompt: Question: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with a rash on the scalp characterized by greasy, yellow scales. The nurse should document this finding as which of the following?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap) (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: Medical records reveal that this client has a history of schizophrenia. Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate from the primary healthcare provider (PHCP) based on the history and physical?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Lorazepam (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Central vision loss (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

**Clinical Judgment Priority:** Always assess the client first when vital signs or acute symptoms change, unless immediate life-saving intervention (airway clearance, oxygen, chest compressions, or stopping an offending infusion) is required first.

items: Bipolar disorder is characterized by extreme changes in mood, energy, and the ability to function.
The classifications include bipolar I disorder, bipolar II disorder, cyclothymic disorder, and mixed features.
Bipolar I disorder: Most severe form, characterized by severe mood episodes from mania to depression
Bipolar II disorder: A milder form of mood elevation; there are milder episodes of hypomania that alternate with periods of severe depression.
Depression affects feelings, thoughts, and behaviors. Depression is one of the most common psychiatric disorders.
Monitor for general hygiene and self-care deficits; may indicate worsening depression.

ECT is a treatment for depression (not a cure). A small amount of an electrical current is delivered through electrodes attached to the temples that cause a brief seizure within the brain; outward movement is usually a slight movement of the hands, feet, or a toe, because premedication is given to relax the muscles. In addition, a short-acting anesthetic is given.

Schizophrenia is a group of mental health problems characterized by psychotic features (hallucinations and delusions), disordered thought processes, and disrupted interpersonal relationships. Disturbances in affect, mood, behavior, and thought processes occur.
Intervention for Schizophrenia
1.Anorexia nervosa; Onset often is associated with a stressful life event. Intensely fears obesity. Body image is distorted, and a disturbed self-concept is common
15. Assess and limit the client’s activity level (anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa).
14.Alcohol Withdrawal

items: Delirium tremens: The state of delirium usually peaks 48 to 72 hours after cessation or reduction of intake (although it can occur later) and lasts 2 to 3 days

Rationale: A client with depression often is withdrawn while experiencing difficulty concentrating, loss of interest or pleasure, low energy, fatigue, and feelings of worthlessness and poor self-esteem. The plan of care needs to provide successful experiences in a stimulating yet structured environment. The remaining options are either too “restrictive” or offer little or no structure and stimulation.

Rationale: The avoidant personality disorder is characterized by social withdrawal and extreme sensitivity to potential rejection. The person retreats to social isolation. Borderline personality disorder is characterized by unstable mood and self-image and impulsive and unpredictable behavior. Schizotypal personality disorder is characterized by the display of abnormal thoughts, perceptions, speech, and behaviors. Obsessive compulsive personality disorder is characterized by perfectionism, the need to control others, and a devotion to work.
Effective for depression with anxiety features as well as depression with psychomotor agitation
d. Altered mental state (delirium)
Block the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin at the presynaptic junction; used to treat depression

Clients who have depression and have not responded to other antidepressant therapies, including electroconvulsive therapy, may be given MAOIs. These medications are not the first choice because of other available medications and the possible serious side and adverse effects that can occur

Side and adverse effects- Polyuria, Polydipsia, Edema, Dysrhythmia , Anorexia, nausea, Dry mouth, mild thirst, Abdominal bloating , Soft stools or diarrhea 9. Fine hand tremors, Inability to concentrate, Muscle weakness, Headache Hypothyroidism and goiter
Improve the thought processes and behavior of the client with psychotic symptoms, especially clients with schizophrenia

Typical antipsychotics are more effective for positive symptoms of schizophrenia, such as hallucinations, aggression, and delusions; these medications also block the chemoreceptor trigger zone and vomiting center in the brain, producing an antiemetic effect.

blocks.text: **Psychopharmacology: SSRIs, MAOIs, Lithium, Antipsychotics (NMS/EPS)** is a core competency within **Week 16: Psychiatric Mental Health, Crisis Care & Psychotherapeutic Medications** for the Next-Generation NCLEX-RN (NGN). This lesson synthesizes high-yield pathophysiology, bedside nursing priorities, pharmacology safety, and test-taking rules triangulated across **Saunders Comprehensive Review (9th Ed.)**, **Kaplan NCLEX-RN Prep**, and **LaCharity Prioritization, Delegation, and Assignment**.

**Clinical Judgment Priority:** Always assess the client first when vital signs or acute symptoms change, unless immediate life-saving intervention (airway clearance, oxygen, chest compressions, or stopping an offending infusion) is required first.

items: Risk factors include genetic predisposition, dysregulation of serotonin and/or norepinephrine, inflammatory processes, stressful or traumatic life events, and various psychological factors.
1.Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)
Inhibit serotonin uptake and elicit an antidepressant response.
1.Monitor vital signs, because SSRIs can potentially lower or elevate blood pressure.
2.Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors

Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRI) are similar to SSRIs, but they also work by blocking the effects of norepinephrine in addition to serotonin. Considerations are similar to that of SSRIs.
Block the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin at the presynaptic junction; used to treat depression
4.Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors (MAOIs)
Monoamine oxidase metabolizes amines (dopamine, tyramine), norepinephrine, and serotonin, so the concentration of these amines increases with MAOIs.

Clients who have depression and have not responded to other antidepressant therapies, including electroconvulsive therapy, may be given MAOIs. These medications are not the first choice because of other available medications and the possible serious side and adverse effects that can occur
10. Teach the client about foods that contain tyramine. Consuming tyramine-containing foods when taking an MAOI can cause hypertensive crisis.

blocks.title: Psychopharmacology: SSRIs, MAOIs, Lithium, Antipsychotics (NMS/EPS) — Quick Clinical Decision Table
rows: **Acute Cue Recognition**
Assess ABCs, mental status, SpO2, and perfusion trends immediately.
Do NOT delegate unstable assessment to UAP or delay airway support for routine paperwork.
**Medication & IV Safety**
Verify target lab values, allergies, and infusion compatibility before administration.
Never give K+-wasting diuretics if K+ < 3.5 mEq/L without holding/clarifying; check apical HR < 60 before Digoxin.
**Delegation (RN/LPN/UAP)**
RN: Initial assessment, teaching, unstable clients, IV push. LPN: Stable meds/dressings. UAP: Routine vitals & ADLs.
Watch for words like 'newly admitted', 'post-op day 0', or 'unstable' — keep those with the RN.

items: 8. Instruct the client not to adjust the dosage or stop the medication without consulting the PHCP, because lithium should be tapered and not discontinued abruptly.
9. Instruct the client about the signs and symptoms of lithium toxicity.
Occurs when ingested lithium cannot be detoxified and excreted by the kidneys b. Symptoms of toxicity begin to appear when the serum lithium level is at 1.5 mEq/L (1.5 mmol/L).
Interventions for lithium toxicity
Withhold lithium and notify the PHCP.
Prepare to obtain samples to monitor lithium, electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine levels and perform a complete blood cell count.

quiz.prompt: The parents of a child diagnosed with sickle cell disease ask how they can prevent a crisis. What is the nurse's best response?
options: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures."
"Your child should avoid all physical activity."
"Give your child aspirin if they complain of pain."
"Make sure your child eats a high-fat diet."
quiz.rationale: Correct option: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following interventions would be most beneficial for this patient?
quiz.rationale: Increased fluid intake can help thin out thick secretions in the lungs, making them easier to cough up and improving oxygenation.

quiz.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a corticosteroid inhaler and a bronchodilator inhaler. How should these medications be administered?
options: The bronchodilator should be used, followed by the corticosteroid
The corticosteroid should be used, followed by the bronchodilator
Both inhalers should be used simultaneously
The order of administration does not matter
quiz.rationale: The bronchodilator should be administered first to open the airways, allowing the corticosteroid to be more effectively delivered and absorbed.

quiz.prompt: Question: A child with idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) is admitted to the hospital. Which intervention should be included in the child's care plan?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Monitoring for signs of bleeding (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A patient with heart failure is experiencing shortness of breath. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Administer oxygen (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant on a pediatric oncology unit. Which task is appropriate to delegate?
options: Discussing the side effects of chemotherapy with a patient's parents
Administering oral pain medication to a child with bone cancer
Assisting a child with leukemia with bathing and dressing
Assessing a child's response to a blood transfusion
quiz.rationale: Option C is an appropriate task to delegate to a nursing assistant as it falls within their scope of practice. Options A, B, and D involve patient education, medication administration, and assessment, respectively, which are within the nurse's scope of practice and should not be delegated.

quiz.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis is started on a regimen of multiple antibiotics. What should the nurse include in patient teaching regarding this treatment?
options: The patient will need to be on antibiotics for several weeks
The patient should expect a rapid improvement in symptoms
The patient should not drink alcohol while on these medications
quiz.rationale: Tuberculosis requires a prolonged treatment with multiple antibiotics, often for several months. The patient should be cautioned not to drink alcohol while on these medications due to potential for liver damage. It's also important to inform the patient that although they might feel better, they need to finish the full course of antibiotics to fully treat the infection.

quiz.prompt: A patient with hypoparathyroidism is experiencing seizures. What is the nurse's first action?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Administer calcium supplements (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A client with pneumonia is prescribed incentive spirometry. What is the rationale for this intervention?
options: To assess the client's respiratory rate
To measure the client's peak expiratory flow rate
To improve the client's lung expansion and prevent atelectasis
To monitor the client's oxygen saturation levels
quiz.rationale: Incentive spirometry is used to improve lung expansion, prevent atelectasis (collapse of the lung), and promote deep breathing. It helps to improve ventilation and oxygenation, especially in clients with pneumonia who may have decreased lung function

quiz.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is experiencing dry skin and hair loss. What is the nurse's first action?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Increase levothyroxine dose (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A patient with acromegaly is taking octreotide. What is the primary goal of treatment?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Decrease growth hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been prescribed a liquid medication. The prescription calls for 5 mL to be given twice daily. The parents are unsure how to measure this amount. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Use a teaspoon from the kitchen.
Use the dropper that came with the medication.
Use a syringe without a needle.
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Use a syringe without a needle. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is administering eardrops to an adult client. Which of the following is the correct method?
options: Instil the drops directly onto the eardrum
Instil the drops onto the wall of the ear canal
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted towards the affected ear
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted away from the affected ear
quiz.rationale: When administering eardrops, the client's head should be tilted so that the affected ear is facing upward. This allows the medication to travel down the ear canal. Options A and B are incorrect because the drops should not be instilled directly onto the eardrum or the wall of the ear canal as this can cause discomfort and potentially damage the eardrum. Option C is incorrect because tilting the head towards the affected ear may cause the medication to drain out of the ear canal.

quiz.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is 2 days post-op from a thoracotomy. The patient is reluctant to perform deep breathing exercises due to pain. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement?
options: Administer pain medication before the exercises
Encourage shallow breathing to prevent discomfort
Discontinue the exercises until the pain subsides
Encourage the patient to hold their breath as long as possible
quiz.rationale: Deep breathing exercises are critical after thoracotomy to prevent complications such as pneumonia and atelectasis. Administering pain medication before the exercises can help alleviate the patient's discomfort and encourage compliance.

quiz.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is taking methimazole. What is the primary goal of treatment?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Increase thyroid hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A child with osteosarcoma reports pain in the affected leg. The nurse has delegated the administration of oral pain medication to a nursing assistant. What is the most appropriate action by the nurse?
options: The nurse should administer the medication instead
The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration
The nurse should instruct the nursing assistant to assess the child's pain level
The nurse should document the administration of the medication
quiz.rationale: The nurse cannot delegate the administration of medication or the assessment of pain to a nursing assistant. These tasks fall within the nurse's scope of practice. The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration to determine the effectiveness of the medication.

quiz.prompt: Question: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with a rash on the scalp characterized by greasy, yellow scales. The nurse should document this finding as which of the following?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap) (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: Medical records reveal that this client has a history of schizophrenia. Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate from the primary healthcare provider (PHCP) based on the history and physical?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Lorazepam (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
quiz.rationale: Correct option: Central vision loss (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a patient with a tracheostomy. Which of the following instructions should the nurse provide to the patient to prevent complications?
questions.rationale: Regular coughing and deep breathing exercises can help to clear secretions from the lungs and maintain a patent airway, reducing the risk of complications such as pneumonia.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a 4-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to observe?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Fatigue and frequent infections (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of hyperglycemia. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer insulin (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

options: Providing patient education about the disease

questions.rationale: Correct option: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child with celiac disease. Which dietary instruction is most appropriate?
options: The child should avoid foods containing gluten.
The child should follow a low-protein diet.
The child should consume a high-fat diet.
The child should increase intake of dairy products.
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is an autoimmune disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Avoiding gluten is the primary treatment. Options B, C, and D are not typically recommended for children with celiac disease.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute. The patient is lethargic and unresponsive. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Position the patient on their side
questions.rationale: A respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute is dangerously low and indicates respiratory failure. The patient is unresponsive, suggesting a lack of oxygen to the brain. Immediate intervention, such as intubation, is needed.

questions.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant on a pediatric oncology unit. Which task is appropriate to delegate?
options: Discussing the side effects of chemotherapy with a patient's parents
Administering oral pain medication to a child with bone cancer
Assisting a child with leukemia with bathing and dressing
Assessing a child's response to a blood transfusion
questions.rationale: Option C is an appropriate task to delegate to a nursing assistant as it falls within their scope of practice. Options A, B, and D involve patient education, medication administration, and assessment, respectively, which are within the nurse's scope of practice and should not be delegated.

questions.prompt: A patient with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is intubated and receiving mechanical ventilation. The nurse notices a sudden drop in the patient's oxygen saturation. What should the nurse do first?
options: Increase the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) on the ventilator
Check the ventilator tubing for disconnection or kinks
questions.rationale: The nurse should first check for any mechanical causes of decreased oxygen saturation, such as a disconnection or kinks in the ventilator tubing, which could compromise ventilation.

questions.prompt: who practices Orthodox Judaism and keeps a kosher diet?
options: Broiled chicken with rice, vegetables and mixed fruit
Pasta with shrimp and cream sauce with salad, fruit and coffee
Shrimp salad on a roll with potato salad and pickled beets
Pork chops with baked potato, fruit cup and milk
questions.rationale: Correct option: Broiled chicken with rice, vegetables and mixed fruit (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The charge nurse is delegating tasks for the day. Which of the following tasks can be delegated to a nursing assistant?
options: Assisting a patient with personal hygiene
questions.rationale: Correct option: Assisting a patient with personal hygiene (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The nurse hears continuous, dry, low-pitched breath sounds on auscultation. What could this indicate?
questions.rationale: Continuous, dry, low-pitched breath sounds are characteristic of bronchitis. This sound, also known as rhonchi, is caused by air passing through narrowed or partially obstructed airways.

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child with asthma has been prescribed a metered-dose inhaler (MDI). The child is having difficulty coordinating inhalation with medication release. What is the best recommendation the nurse can make?
options: Try using a different type of inhaler.
Use a spacer with the MDI.
Practice more until the child gets it right.
Have a parent administer the medication.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Use a spacer with the MDI. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with a suspected diagnosis of Meniere's disease. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to find?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Tinnitus (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 4-year-old child is admitted to the hospital for treatment of pneumonia. Which nursing intervention would be most appropriate to help the child cope with the hospitalization?
options: Encourage the child to participate in care activities
Keep the child in bed to promote rest
Limit parental visitation to prevent overstimulation
Avoid talking about the hospitalization with the child
questions.rationale: Correct option: Encourage the child to participate in care activities (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a chest tube connected to an underwater seal drainage system. Which of the following indicates a properly functioning system?
options: Constant bubbling in the water seal chamber
No fluctuations in the water seal chamber
Drainage system is kept at the level of the patient's chest
Fluctuations in the water seal chamber with respirations
questions.rationale: Normal functioning of an underwater seal drainage system is indicated by fluctuations (rising with inspiration and falling with expiration) in the water seal chamber with respirations.

questions.prompt: A patient with pheochromocytoma is experiencing hypertension and tachycardia. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease catecholamine production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Question: A nurse is teaching a group of parents about growth hormone deficiency in children. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: It results in accelerated growth and development.
It is usually diagnosed during adolescence.
It can lead to short stature if left untreated.
questions.rationale: Correct option: It results in accelerated growth and development. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A healthcare worker experiences hives and itching after using latex gloves. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Latex allergy (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is experiencing thyroid nodules. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease thyroid hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The RN is delegating tasks to a licensed practical nurse (LPN). Which of the following tasks is appropriate for the RN to delegate to the LPN?
options: Monitoring a patient's response to medications
questions.rationale: Correct option: Monitoring a patient's response to medications (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

options: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures."
"Your child should avoid all physical activity."
"Give your child aspirin if they complain of pain."
"Make sure your child eats a high-fat diet."
questions.rationale: Correct option: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching safety precautions to a client with a hearing impairment. Which of the following should be included in the teaching plan?
options: Install smoke detectors with strobe lights
questions.rationale: Correct option: Install smoke detectors with strobe lights (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted to the hospital with a cardiac tamponade. Which of the following signs and symptoms should the nurse expect to observe?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Hypotension and jugular venous distension (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient has just undergone enucleation of the eye due to ocular melanoma. What is the nurse's priority in the immediate postoperative care of this patient?
options: Ensuring the patient's pain is controlled
Educating the patient about the use of an ocular prosthesis
Monitoring the surgical site for bleeding
Providing emotional support to the patient
questions.rationale: While all of these actions are important, the nurse's immediate postoperative priority is to monitor the surgical site for bleeding or other complications. Pain control, patient education about an ocular prosthesis, and emotional support will follow once the patient is medically stable.

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperparathyroidism is experiencing bone pain. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease calcium levels (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is experiencing increased dyspnoea and wheezing. Which intervention should the nurse prioritize?
questions.rationale: In a client with COPD experiencing increased dyspnea and wheezing, administering a bronchodilator medication can help to open the airways and improve breathing. Bronchodilators work by relaxing the muscles around the airways, making it easier for the client to breathe.

questions.prompt: A patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been admitted to the hospital. Which of the following findings would the nurse expect to observe during the assessment?
questions.rationale: Patients with COPD often have difficulty exhaling, leading to a prolonged expiratory phase. The other options are not typical findings in COPD.

questions.prompt: A client with pneumonia is prescribed incentive spirometry. What is the rationale for this intervention?
options: To assess the client's respiratory rate
To measure the client's peak expiratory flow rate
To improve the client's lung expansion and prevent atelectasis
To monitor the client's oxygen saturation levels
questions.rationale: Incentive spirometry is used to improve lung expansion, prevent atelectasis (collapse of the lung), and promote deep breathing. It helps to improve ventilation and oxygenation, especially in clients with pneumonia who may have decreased lung function

questions.prompt: A patient with Addison's disease is experiencing hypotension and dehydration. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer hydrocortisone (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Question: A 2-year-old patient is suspected of having iron-deficiency anemia. Which symptom is most likely to be observed?
options: Yellowing of the skin and eyes
questions.rationale: Correct option: Rapid heart rate (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who had a laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) procedure. Which of the following is a priority nursing responsibility in the immediate postoperative period?
options: Encouraging the patient to blink frequently
Protecting the patient’s eyes from injury
questions.rationale: After LASIK surgery, it's crucial to protect the eyes from any potential injury. The patient's corneas have been reshaped and need time to heal. While administering antibiotic eye drops is also important, it is not the immediate priority.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care?
options: Use sterile technique when suctioning the tracheostomy
Encourage the client to cough and deep breathe every 2 hours
questions.rationale: All the listed interventions are part of the appropriate care for a client with a tracheostomy. They all help maintain a patent airway, promote effective gas exchange, and prevent infection.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer a bronchodilator to a client with asthma. Which of the following outcomes would indicate that the medication has been effective?
options: The client's pulse oximetry reading is 92%
The client is able to speak in full sentences
The client's respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute
The client's peak flow reading has decreased
questions.rationale: The ability to speak in full sentences without becoming short of breath indicates that the bronchodilator is effective and the client's airway obstruction is improving.

questions.prompt: Medical records reveal that this client has a history of schizophrenia. Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate from the primary healthcare provider (PHCP) based on the history and physical?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Levodopa-Carbidopa← Parkinson?!?! (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient who may have a perforated eardrum. Which of the following symptoms would likely be present?
questions.rationale: A perforated eardrum can cause ringing in the ears (tinnitus), sudden cessation of ear pain (as the pressure is relieved by the perforation), and hearing loss. Therefore, all of these symptoms might be present if a patient has a perforated eardrum.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been prescribed a liquid medication. The prescription calls for 5 mL to be given twice daily. The parents are unsure how to measure this amount. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Use a teaspoon from the kitchen.
Use the dropper that came with the medication.
Use a syringe without a needle.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Use a syringe without a needle. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A mechanically ventilated patient has a respiratory rate of 35 breaths per minute. The ventilator is set to deliver 12 breaths per minute. What action should the nurse take?
options: Increase the ventilator rate to match the patient's rate
Sedate the patient to decrease the respiratory rate
Assess the patient for causes of increased respiratory rate
questions.rationale: The patient may be breathing above the ventilator rate due to hypoxia, pain, anxiety, or other reasons. The nurse should assess the patient to identify and address the cause.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following interventions would be most beneficial for this patient?
questions.rationale: Increased fluid intake can help thin out thick secretions in the lungs, making them easier to cough up and improving oxygenation.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer montelukast to a patient with asthma. The nurse should inform the patient that this medication has which of the following therapeutic effects?
options: It thins and loosens mucus in the airways
It reduces inflammation in the airways
questions.rationale: Montelukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist. It works by blocking leukotrienes, substances in the body that cause inflammation and constriction in the airways and production of mucus.

questions.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following tasks can the nurse safely delegate?
options: Evaluating the patient's response to treatment
questions.rationale: Encouraging fluid intake can be safely delegated to a nursing assistant. The other tasks require nursing judgement and should be performed by the nurse.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is 2 days post-op from a thoracotomy. The patient is reluctant to perform deep breathing exercises due to pain. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement?
options: Administer pain medication before the exercises
Encourage shallow breathing to prevent discomfort
Discontinue the exercises until the pain subsides
Encourage the patient to hold their breath as long as possible
questions.rationale: Deep breathing exercises are critical after thoracotomy to prevent complications such as pneumonia and atelectasis. Administering pain medication before the exercises can help alleviate the patient's discomfort and encourage compliance.

questions.prompt: What type of heart failure does this statement describe? The ventricle is unable to properly fill with blood because it is too stiff. Therefore, blood backs up into the lungs causing the patient to experience shortness of breath.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is diagnosed with cardiogenic shock. Which of the following interventions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Monitoring vital signs and cardiac output
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administering oxygen and vasopressors (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing dietary education to the parents of a child with celiac disease. Which food should the nurse instruct the parents to eliminate from the child's diet?
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Gluten is found in wheat, rye, and barley. Therefore, wheat should be eliminated from the diet of a child with celiac disease. Rice (option A), corn (option C), and potatoes (option D) are naturally gluten-free and can be included in the diet.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient post bronchoscopy. Which of the following is the most important assessment before offering the patient food or drink?
questions.rationale: After a bronchoscopy, the patient’s throat may be numb from local anaesthetics used during the procedure. It is essential to ensure the return of the gag reflex before offering food or drink to prevent aspiration.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Central vision loss (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching the parents of a 1-year-old child with eczema about skin care. Which of the following should be included in the teaching?
options: Bathe the child daily with hot water and soap
Apply a moisturizer to the child's skin while it's still damp
Dress the child in wool or synthetic fabrics
Use perfumed lotions to soothe the skin
questions.rationale: Correct option: Apply a moisturizer to the child's skin while it's still damp (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is administering eardrops to an adult client. Which of the following is the correct method?
options: Instil the drops directly onto the eardrum
Instil the drops onto the wall of the ear canal
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted towards the affected ear
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted away from the affected ear
questions.rationale: When administering eardrops, the client's head should be tilted so that the affected ear is facing upward. This allows the medication to travel down the ear canal. Options A and B are incorrect because the drops should not be instilled directly onto the eardrum or the wall of the ear canal as this can cause discomfort and potentially damage the eardrum. Option C is incorrect because tilting the head towards the affected ear may cause the medication to drain out of the ear canal.

questions.prompt: A patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) is experiencing symptoms of medullary thyroid cancer. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease calcium levels (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of sharp, severe chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient's blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, heart rate is 120 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 90%. What should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: The patient's symptoms of sudden onset of severe chest pain, shortness of breath, tachycardia, hypotension, and low oxygen saturation are indicative of a pulmonary embolism, a life-threatening emergency.

questions.prompt: A child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is receiving chemotherapy. What should the nurse closely monitor for in this patient?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Hypertension (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child weighing 20 kg is scheduled to receive a dose of medication. The medication is ordered at a dose of 5 mg/kg/dose every 8 hours. The medication comes in a concentration of 100 mg/5 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 2 mL (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with type 1 diabetes is experiencing hyperglycemia. Which medication would the nurse administer?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Regular insulin (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of gastroparesis. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer metoclopramide (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
questions.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

questions.prompt: A mother brings her 3-year-old child to the clinic with a rash on the child's back. The rash is made up of fluid-filled vesicles that are clustered together. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Chickenpox (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).
